text:
maria: heads up — after a cluster scale event in eu-west-1, pods in nodepool-a lost egress to S3 via our interface endpoint (private DNS enabled). app requests get connection refused or DNS NODATA. anyone seeing this?
ben: seeing it from canary nodes too. curious that only endpoint-backed services are affected, internet egress via NAT is fine.
samir: grabbing kube-proxy/containerd logs now. saw lots of conntrack delete/replace around the scale event:
```
Feb 18 10:02:11 node-17 kube-proxy[...]: conntrack: NAT deletion for src=10.2.12.34:43122 dst=52.95.123.45:443
Feb 18 10:02:11 node-17 kube-proxy[...]: conntrack: no route for dst 52.95.123.45
```
katie: I pulled the ENI list for the interface endpoint (vpce-0abcde): some ENIs detached+reattached across AZs during autoscaler churn. SGs attached look fine (allow 443 from our subnets). output snippet:
```
ENI eni-0aa1  attached subnet subnet-a (eu-west-1a)
ENI eni-0bb2  attached subnet subnet-b (eu-west-1b)
```
ben: DNS looks weird too — from a pod: `dig +short s3.dualstack.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` returns empty. coredns logs show forwarding to 169.254.169.253 (VPC resolver) with no answer.
maria: interface endpoints use private hosted zone automatic resolve. If ENI moves AZ, the VPC resolver should still answer. Could be a stale route cache or conntrack sticking to old ENI IP and the ENI moved, so packets hitting wrong ENI get RST/NACK.
samir: did tcpdump on node-17 to the endpoint IP (52.95.123.45 is an example) — saw SYN then immediate RST with src IP equal to old ENI: `14:02:11.123456 IP 10.2.12.34.43122 > 52.95.123.45.443: Flags [S], seq 12345
14:02:11.123457 IP 52.95.123.45.443 > 10.2.12.34.43122: Flags [R], seq 0`
katie: think automation (our subnet reclamation job) reassigned the route table for that subnet to a shared RT that had different main association and somehow triggered AWS to move endpoint ENIs? Not sure but correlation strong with automation run.
ben: quick repro: restart a node (drain) -> when it comes back some pods can't talk to vpce for a few minutes until conntrack ages out. Restarting kube-proxy clears it immediately.
maria: short-term mitigation — roll restart kube-proxy on affected node pool + add iptables rule to flush conntrack for endpoint IPs. longer-term: we should pin endpoint ENIs per-az and disable the automation that swaps route tables during scale windows.
samir: flush command we used: `sudo conntrack -D -d 52.95.123.45` (or `conntrack -D --orig-dst 52.95.123.45`). doing that on node fixed a pod in ~2s.
katie: also verified Route53 private DNS entries for the endpoint are present. So DNS appears fine; the traffic path broken when ENI IPs change while conntrack still references old mapping.
ben: opened a PR to include conntrack flush in our node reboot handler and to add a pre-scale hook to gracefully migrate ENIs.
maria: deployed the kube-proxy restart and conntrack flush as a temporary runbook, rolling now. will keep NAT fallback policy as plan B if this reoccurs.
sre-bot: :rotating_light: created incident INC-2026-103 (owner: eng-infra) — tracking mitigation and permanent fix.
maria: thanks. follow-up tasks: 1) disable route-table reassignment automation in scale windows 2) implement ENI pinning by AZ for interface endpoints 3) add conntrack-flush step to node lifecycle playbook.
ben: +1 :thumbsup:
katie: will open infra tickets and a postmortem template once stabilized.
